A.name: Baseline: GSD map plus self-found files
A.description: The agent reads the repository GSD codebase map (generated at the task parent when the repository carries none there) and finds any other files itself with ordinary search and reads. No AVARICE pack. This is the D-06 baseline, taken from docs/operations-and-testing.md, not the full repository.

B.name: Pack with the code-only graph
B.description: The AVARICE context pack built at the task parent with the gsd-intel and gsd-graph adapters, the knowledge pass off: code nodes only.

C.name: Pack with the knowledge graph
C.description: The same pack with the knowledge pass on: code nodes plus document nodes.

specMapping: The spec names three arms: document section reads, the code-only graph, and the graph with document nodes (docs/operations-and-testing.md, Context retrieval evaluation). Here arm A is the D-06 baseline, B is the code-only graph and C is the graph with document nodes. The difference from the spec is recorded as a findings line by plan 04-39.
successRule: A task succeeds when every required check passes at the end of the run and the held-out test, copied from the target commit after the agent finishes, passes. Reviewer judgment is a sampled owner spot-check, not a gate.

passRule.text: AC-8 passes when the task success rate of arm B or arm C is at least the success rate of arm A and its total tokens are no more than 50% of arm A total tokens, over the 20 tasks.

knowledgeRule.text: D-08: the knowledge pass stays on unless arm C shows no task-success gain over arm B and also costs more tokens than arm B. The outcome is recorded as an ADR in docs/decisions/ either way.

tokenMetric.text: Tokens are the sum, over distinct assistant messages, of input, cache-creation, cache-read and output tokens (A2). USD cost is recorded beside them.

isolation.text: Each arm runs in a checkout at the task parent with no history after it and no remote. The held-out test files are never placed where an arm can read them: deniedReads takes precedence over allowedReads, and the held-out tests are copied in only after the agent has stopped. The index and the pack are built at the parent, never at the target commit.

tasks.subject: fix(03): WR-04 drop the Identity cache after a failed write so a lost reply cannot cause an overwrite
tasks.brief:
fix(03): WR-04 drop the Identity cache after a failed write so a lost reply cannot cause an overwrite

write_identity planned later writes from a cache that follows only requests whose reply arrived. A request Google applied whose reply was lost left
the cache behind the sheet, and the next write rewrote the cell without the entries already written (or appended a second row for the same chunk).
Any exception now drops the cache and the next call reads the Identity tab alone before planning.

tasks.subject: fix(03): WR-03 carry a failed Tally row in the storage key so a transient write error is not a permanent undercount
tasks.brief:
fix(03): WR-03 carry a failed Tally row in the storage key so a transient write error is not a permanent undercount

In compact mode a run's baseline counts live only in its Tally row, so the start-of-run repair cannot rebuild them. A failed append now keeps the
row (counts only, at most 20) as pending_tally in the storage key; the next run writes it before any repair, drops it if the group is already
in Tally, and keeps the repair from writing a shorter row for a waiting group. SPEC and DECISIONS D-57 updated.

tasks.subject: Gate ASR on caption-sufficiency, same as OCR (fixes ASR OOM on the common path)
tasks.brief:
Gate ASR on caption-sufficiency, same as OCR (fixes ASR OOM on the common path)

Product-scope decision (2026-07-20): this app's actual scope is ingredients
-> cart, not step-by-step cooking instructions. Narration's two roles were
(a) capturing `steps` - confirmed unused, never rendered anywhere in web/
- and (b) a secondary tie-breaking evidence source for ingredient values
when OCR/caption conflict (reconcile.ts rules 3/9). Neither justifies
running Whisper unconditionally on every job when the caption already
covers ingredients, especially given the real cost: ASR inference peaks
~1.3-2GB RSS for realistic audio (see recipecart-worker-asr-oom memory),
exceeding the Railway worker's 1024MB limit and OOM-crashing every real
job, including caption-sufficient ones.

Fix: transcribeAudio() is now gated by the same `extractFrames` flag OCR
already uses (both derive from captionSufficient). Caption-sufficient
jobs - the common case, and per this session's explicit working
assumption - now skip ASR entirely and never touch the OOM-prone code
path. Caption-insufficient jobs still run both OCR and ASR, so the known
memory issue remains open for that path specifically - deferred, not
fixed, matching this session's decision to treat caption-sufficient
extraction as the thing that needs to be solid for now.

tasks.subject: Fix real duplicate-detection gap: resolve short-link tokens before dedup
tasks.brief:
Fix real duplicate-detection gap: resolve short-link tokens before dedup

Real gap found via live iOS Shortcut testing 2026-07-20: TikTok's native
Share button mints a fresh tiktok.com/t/<token>/ short-link every time,
even for the identical underlying video. Job-creation dedup was keyed on
the raw URL string (or a video id parsed directly from the URL shape),
but normalizeUrl() can't extract an id from short-link forms at all -
that only happens later, inside yt-dlp, well after job creation. So two
shares of the exact same video almost never actually deduped in practice,
only when a user happened to paste the literal identical URL string
twice - not the common real-world case.

Fix: deriveIdempotencyKey (src/platform/jobs.ts) now resolves short-link
redirect chains via a lightweight HEAD request (resolveShortLinkVideoId,
normalize_url.ts) before computing the dedup key, extracting the real
video id. Only fires for short-link forms - full-form /video/<id> submits
are unaffected, so this adds no latency to the common case. Falls back to
raw-URL dedup on any resolution failure (network hiccup, timeout - capped
at config.jobs.shortLinkResolveTimeoutMs, 2.5s) rather than failing the
submission.

Verified against real TikTok servers, not just mocks: resolved a real
short-link to its actual video id in ~586ms, and confirmed end-to-end via
the real compiled API that a short-link submit and a full-form submit of
the same video now correctly collapse into one job (created: false on
the second).

Also resolves docs/ios-shortcut.md's stale "/setup path is a guess" open
question - confirmed live and working this session.

tasks.subject: Phase 2: escalation-scoring refinement (Spec 2 §2.4)
tasks.brief:
Phase 2: escalation-scoring refinement (Spec 2 §2.4)

The P1 baseline scored escalation frames by ingredient-likelihood alone.
Adds the two other terms the spec calls for:
- Inverse-OCR-confidence weighting: a frame Tesseract read with LOW
  confidence but that still looks like an ingredient line is exactly the
  case vision escalation exists for. A floor (0.2) keeps a fully-confident
  read from being zeroed out — still useful evidence, just less urgent to
  also send as an image.
- Early-frame bonus: a flat, linearly-decaying bonus for frames near the
  start of the video (ordinal extracted from the frame_ref's embedded
  index — media_split's frame-NNN.jpg / resize_frames's resized-NNN.jpg
  both encode video-time order).
- Hard rule: the single earliest-ordinal frame is always included even if
  its own score doesn't make the ranked cut — a title/ingredient card
  doesn't always contain quantity/unit-shaped text the likelihood scorer
  recognizes. This is a real, documented behavior change from P1: a lone
  frame with zero ingredient-likelihood text is now force-included as the
  only (hence earliest) candidate rather than dropped — escalate_select.test.ts
  updated with the new expectation and a comment explaining why.

tasks.subject: Phase 2: search staleness re-check before cart approval (Spec 3 §2.2, A3-6)
tasks.brief:
Phase 2: search staleness re-check before cart approval (Spec 3 §2.2, A3-6)

"Re-run search if the recipe has sat in awaiting_review past a config
window... before a cart run uses its prices." config.kroger.searchStalenessWindowMs
(24h default) already existed but nothing enforced it.

- matcher/index.ts: isMatchStale(recipeId) checks the OLDEST persisted
  product_matches.updated_at across a recipe's ingredients (a partial
  per-ingredient refresh isn't meaningful — matchRecipeAndPersist always
  re-matches every ingredient in one pass). refreshIfStale() re-runs
  matching only when stale, a no-op otherwise (no extra Kroger calls in the
  common case of approving promptly after extraction).
- cli.ts's `approve` command calls refreshIfStale before selecting approved
  items — also fixes a latent gap where `approve` never loaded the store
  location at all, so it had no locationId available for a re-search even
  if one were needed.

Live-verified a real parsing gotcha before shipping: sqlite's
datetime('now') returns a UTC string with no 'Z'/'T' markers
("2026-07-19 01:41:19"), and `new Date(thatString)` parses it as LOCAL
time, not UTC — a real ~5h skew in this environment's timezone that would
have silently misjudged staleness. parseSqliteUtcDatetime() converts to a
proper ISO string first. staleness.test.ts uses a real in-memory sqlite DB
(not the generic mocked-statement stub the rest of index.test.ts uses)
specifically so this date math is exercised for real, not assumed correct.

tasks.subject: Fix cart:approve never updating the parent job's status
tasks.brief:
Fix cart:approve never updating the parent job's status

Real bug, caught live via a real approved cart run: runCartApproval only
ever wrote to cart_runs (its own table) - nothing updated the parent jobs
row. The web app's CartProgress screen polls GET /recipes/:id (i.e.
jobs.status) waiting for a terminal completed/partially_completed value
to know when to navigate to the itemized CartResult screen. Since jobs
never left awaiting_review, the real cart run finished successfully in
the backend (verified: a real cart_runs row with status=completed and a
real completed_at) while the frontend just spun on the progress screen
forever with no way to tell the user it was actually done.

Fix: cart.ts's route now calls the same finishJob() helper the worker's
own state machine already uses for terminal transitions.
CartRunStatus's four values (completed/partially_completed/failed/
requires_user_intervention) are identical strings to the matching
JobStatusValue states, and recipeId === jobId always by construction.
